evals.prompt: Set up Hermes for Example Co. We use Notion, Gmail, and Google Drive.
evals.expected_output: Starts from the one stack answer, checks available interaction routes, and drafts one five-surface workspace context rather than generating component skills.
assertions: Does not repeat platform-by-platform usage questions before checking available routes
Names a skill, CLI, or MCP route for each configured platform and distinguishes inventory from connection health
Maps sources into Work, People, Knowledge, Communications, and Decisions
Uses one .hermes.md workspace context and a separate connection receipt
Does not create intermediary company component skills or request credentials in chat

farplane.title: One stack answer produces one workspace draft

evals.prompt: Our delivery work is split between a Notion roadmap and Linear engineering projects. Our company directory is also in Notion. Capture that setup for Hermes.
evals.expected_output: Represents both work systems as separate Work rows and reuses Notion under People without inventing another schema.
assertions: Creates separate Notion and Linear rows under Work
Creates a Notion row under People
Each populated row contains platform, use-via route, source or link, and structural description
Allows one platform to appear under several surfaces
Does not collapse multiple sources into a generated company-work skill

farplane.title: Company surfaces support multiple platform rows

evals.prompt: Add our project system to Hermes. The connector is listed, but opening even one project fails.
evals.expected_output: Keeps the platform blocked in the connection receipt, uses provider-owned authentication, and does not present the workspace route as healthy.
assertions: Does not treat an inventoried skill or connector as a healthy connection
Uses provider-owned authentication rather than asking for credentials
Attempts only the cheapest bounded status and read probes
Records the platform as blocked in the separate receipt
Does not claim representative lookup proof or readiness

farplane.title: Connection failure remains outside workspace context

evals.prompt: Finish the company workspace file now. Leave the Gmail connection for later and make sure the result is safe to load in Hermes.
evals.expected_output: Produces a clean owner-reviewable workspace context, defers Gmail in the receipt, and removes authoring instructions and secrets from the runtime file.
assertions: Keeps Gmail deferred in the receipt rather than describing it as connected in .hermes.md
Removes unresolved company placeholders and ONBOARDING comments from the rendered file
Keeps template metadata with a resolved company name, description, and IANA timezone
Contains no credentials, tokens, private keys, or transient status output
Preserves explicit approval boundaries for consequential writes

farplane.title: Rendered workspace is clean and safe to inject
